feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: What Argentina gets right about youth soccer — and what the U.S. gets wrong
entry.summary: Argentina has produced some of the world's greatest soccer players. Could its youth system offer lessons for the United States?

entry.title: Families of pilgrims likely caught in floods are desperate for news from Nepal
entry.summary: Four days after catastrophic floods wiped out villages along the Nepal-China border, thousands are still missing. Families look for answers but hear nothing.

entry.title: Getting aid to Nepal's flood survivors is the next challenge
entry.summary: The U.S. has pledged 3.5 million in flood aid for Tibet and Nepal, with the first $500,000 distributed by Catholic Relief Services. An aid worker with the group explains what flood survivors need now.

entry.title: Noel Godin, who made powerful people nervous around cream pies, dies at 80
entry.summary: For more than 50 years, Noel Godin went after famous and powerful people with cream pies. His targets included politicians, philosophers, filmmakers and, famously, Bill Gates.

entry.title: What a Brazilian tradition can teach us about the future of psychedelics
entry.summary: Researchers are looking at new ways to use psychedelics to treat depression. Science journalist Marcelo Leite says there's also a lot to learn from indigenous people who have used them for generations.

entry.title: The Ukrainian women disappearing into Russian prisons
entry.summary: What happens when Russia arrests civilians in the Ukrainian territories it occupies? New Yorker writer Joshua Yaffa followed a group of women through the Russian prison system.

entry.title: Canada claps back at Trump's efforts to rename Lake Ontario as 'Lake America'
entry.summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford has unveiled a giant billboard reading: "Lake Ontario — Now and Always." But tech giant Google has said it is renaming the lake for U.S. users, as President Trump demanded.

entry.title: Energy experts have doubts about Trump's newly proposed Venezuelan oil deal
entry.summary: There are many reasons to be skeptical of the Trump administration's announcement that the U.S. will develop Venezuelan oil.

entry.title: From Appalachia to Africa: Why Dolly Parton was beloved across the continent
entry.summary: Dolly Parton's songs traveled far beyond Nashville. Across Africa, musicians embraced her stories of hardship, heartbreak and humble beginnings — and made them their own.

entry.title: Nepal warns of possible fresh flooding as communities grapple with devastation
entry.summary: Authorities in Nepal warned of possible fresh flooding on Sunday and urged residents in flood-affected districts to remain on high alert after water levels rose in the Bhotekoshi River.
